title: Bias and Fairness in Large Language Models: A Survey
benchmark_measurement: Measurement of stereotypes, misrepresentation, and disparate treatment related to religious groups. This includes assessing biased associations (e.g., anti-Muslim bias), biased inferences in religion-polarity contexts, and reliance on stereotypes in ambiguous question-answering scenarios.
findings: This survey paper consolidates findings from existing literature, indicating that Large Language Models can learn, perpetuate, and amplify harmful social biases related to religion, such as anti-Muslim stereotypes. It catalogs various benchmarks and datasets (e.g., StereoSet, CrowS-Pairs, BBQ, Bias NLI) designed to measure these religious biases through tasks like sentence completion, stereotype detection, and inference. The paper also reviews mitigation techniques, like adversarial training and instruction tuning, that can be applied to reduce religious bias, while noting the limitations and challenges of current evaluation and mitigation methods.
